true_positive_items.rationale: WHAT THE FINDING CLAIMS. The rule tests one condition: a route is public, uses a write verb, and declares neither an allowlist registration nor a tenant-skip. WHAT THE EVIDENCE SHOWS. @Public() sits at class level (line 45) and @Post('csp-report') at line 63, so every request to this route reaches the handler without an authenticated principal — that is the precondition, confirmed on decorators, which are behavior, not narration. The file carries no @SkipTenantGuard across its full 99 lines, so the tenant-skip branch of the requirement is unmet in the only channel a gate can read. The header docblock (line 7) and method docblock (lines 53-62) do state why authentication is absent, but a comment is not a declaration: the judge contract bars comments without behavior from discharging a machine-checked requirement, and no scanner, guard, or test consumes that prose. WHAT THE FINDING DOES NOT CLAIM. It does not say this endpoint should require auth. A CSP report-uri must accept credential-less browser POSTs; making it authenticated would make it useless. The defect is that a legitimate exception is undeclared. WHY IT MATTERS AND WHAT BREAKS IF SKIPPED. The gateway's population of unauthenticated write routes is auditable only while every member is registered somewhere a gate reads. Leave one legitimate exception unregistered and the registry stops discriminating: the next @Public() @Post — one that does persist tenant rows — looks identical to this one at scan time, and the reviewer who trusts the registry approves it. That is how a boundary control degrades into decoration. DOWNSTREAM SURFACE. gateway-api's public route boundary, and every later security-boundary scan whose signal depends on the exception set being complete. ROOT-CAUSE REMEDY (tier 3 — make it detectable).
